The induced projective orders of $A$ and $B$ are both $3$. The matrix $AB$ has two positive real reciprocal eigenvalues of distinct moduli, and $A,B$ have no common eigenline.

outputs.exact_statement: There is an algebraic vector bundle $G$ of rank two on $S$ such that, for every positive integer $m$, the bundle $$E_m=f_m^*G\otimes P$$ is ample. There is an integer $m_0$ such that $E_m$ admits no smooth Hermitian metric with strictly Griffiths-positive Chern curvature for every $m\ge m_0$.

The matrices $A,B$ belong to $\mathop{\mathrm{SL}}_2(\mathbb C)$ and satisfy $$\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}A=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}B=1,\qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}(A^{-1}B)=-\sqrt2,\qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}(AB)=1+\sqrt2.$$ The orders of $A$, $B$, and $A^{-1}B$ in $\mathop{\mathrm{SL}}_2(\mathbb C)$ are $6$, $6$, and $8$, respectively. The induced projective orders of $A$ and $B$ are both $3$. The matrix $AB$ has two positive real reciprocal eigenvalues of distinct moduli, and $A,B$ have no common eigenline.
The divisor $D$ has bidegree $(3,3)$ and exactly six singular points, all ordinary transverse intersections of two components. There are no triple intersections.
For every positive integer $m$, the bundle $E_m=f_m^*G\otimes P$ is ample. More precisely, $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P(E_m)}(n)$ is very ample for every even integer $n$ with $n-1\geq3m$.

Let $G$ be a holomorphic vector bundle of positive rank on $S=\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$, and put $F=G^\vee$. Suppose that $f_m^*G\otimes P$ admits a smooth strictly Griffiths-positive Hermitian metric for infinitely many positive integers $m$. Then there is a function $$q:F\longrightarrow [0,\infty)$$ which is plurisubharmonic on the total space, is not identically zero, and has the following property: for every $x\in S$ there is a finite positive semidefinite Hermitian form $H_x$ on $F_x$ such that $$q(x,v)=H_x(v,v)\qquad(v\in F_x).$$ In particular, this fiberwise assertion holds at every base point.

The function in Proposition 6 represents a distributional limit; no convergence of restrictions to a divisor is asserted. The graph identities will instead be evaluated directly in this single everywhere-defined function $q$.

Let $G$ be the bundle of Proposition 4, and put $F=G^\vee$. Suppose that $q:F\to[0,\infty)$ is finite, plurisubharmonic, not identically zero, and a Hermitian quadratic form on every fiber. Then there is a finite, nonnegative, nonzero plurisubharmonic function $a_\bullet$ on $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-b)$, a Hermitian positive semidefinite quadratic on each fiber, such that $$a_\bullet(Mx,M^{\otimes b}v)=a_\bullet(x,v) \qquad(M=A,B)$$ for every $x\in\mathbb P^1$ and $v\in\mathcal O(-b)_x$.
The projective transformations induced by the matrices $A$ and $B$ in [eq:matrices] preserve no nonzero finite positive Borel measure on $\mathbb P^1$.

For the bundle $G$ of Proposition 4, every finite nonnegative plurisubharmonic function on the total space of $F=G^\vee$ whose restriction to each fiber is a Hermitian quadratic form is identically zero.
